newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BAe shows interest in Australia's ADI.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BAe shows interest in Australia's ADI.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc's Australian subsidiary on Tuesday expressed interest in Australian arms maker ADI Ltd, but said it did not expect the government-owned company to be offered for sale any time soon.
A spokeswoman for British Aerospace Australia Ltd said her company knew that ADI might eventually be sold.

"We are of course aware of the rapid consolidation of the world's defence and aerospace companies and are very keen to play a role in whatever changes are necessary here in Australia to ensure that our defence and aerospace industry has a vibrant part to play in the future," she told Reuters.
A spokesman for Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said on Tuesday the Australian government was not looking at an early sale of ADI.
"We are not opposed to the idea but it's not a short-term priority," the spokesman told Reuters.
ADI, formerly Australian Defence Industries, makes ammunition, firearms under licence and other weapons and defence systems, including minehunters.
Over the past few years it has streamlined its operations by closing obsolete factories and a surplus firing range, releasing land that has turned it into a substantial property developer.
Sources familiar with the company's accounts estimated two years ago that it was worth about A$500 million.
The former Labor government was then considering the company's sale but nothing happened before the party lost the March 1996 election to the Liberal-National coalition.
The spokesman said the new government's attitude to selling ADI was not notably different to Labor's.
One government source, who asked not to be named, said ADI's sale would certainly not be announced in the May budget, which will detail government fiscal plans for the year to June 1998.
Analysts say ADI is a difficult asset to sell because the Australian Defence Department is a near-monopoly purchaser for much of the company's output, especially ammunition.
Industry sources say Defence Industry Minister Bronwyn Bishop has expressed doubts about the company's diversification into property development.
